card.name: Co-administration and drug interaction wording
card.fires_on: Words inside or right after the phrase co-administration or concomitant use of two named drugs, such as the middle of etravirine or ritonavir, or the verb after the drug pair. Also fires weakly on trade relations between two countries.

modes.label: Inside antiviral names
modes.description: Middle of drug names like etravirine or ritonavir in a co-administration phrase.
modes.example: Co-administration of etr<<av>>irine and voriconazole significantly increased

modes.label: After a drug pair
modes.description: Linking word or verb after a pair of drugs in an interaction statement.
modes.example: Concomitant administration of CRESEMBA and MMF<< results>> in increase in MMF exposure.

modes.label: Trade between countries
modes.description: Word linking two countries in a bilateral trade sentence.
modes.example: The bilateral trade relations between India<< and>> Japan are built on a range of breath

card.writes: It seems to push toward words about connection or linking between two parties, such as partnerships and integration.
card.plain: It lights up when two drugs are being combined in an interaction statement, and also when two countries are linked in trade.
